verification.note: Confirmed by reading ImageQueryDropTarget.tsx. dragClass is set only when null (:50-52). onDragLeave returns early when dragClass !== 'one_image' (:66), so an upload-class drag that leaves the frame without a drop never calls reset(). reset() runs only in onDrop (:78) and the effect cleanup (:93). The stale 'upload' class then persists, and the next one-image drag is not reclassified (:50 is false), so it gets no overlay and no preventDefault. This violates I8, which says the class is given at dragenter for each drag. It is a silent functional defect in normal use: drag a non-image file in, drag it out, then drag an image. I did not run it.

Confirmed. image-drop-target-desktop.spec.ts:53-57 evaluates `el?.closest('[data-page-frame]') !== null`. When elementFromPoint returns null, `el?.closest(...)` is undefined, and undefined !== null is true, so the hit-test assertion passes vacuously. The events are also sent with dispatchEvent on the frame (:59-61), not by a real CDP drag, so the hit test does not influence them.

specification_compliance: I8: the stale drag class in ImageQueryDropTarget can violate the rule that the action of a drop is the class given at dragenter. This is the F1 case. Nothing else was checked against the invariants.
regression_risks: Resetting dragClass on upload-class dragleave must keep depth counting correct for nested elements inside the frame.
test_coverage: ImageQueryDropTarget.test.tsx covers a one-image drag leaving, but not an upload-class drag leaving followed by a one-image drag. The e2e drop-target spec has a vacuous hit-test assertion.
not_verified: I did not run any test or browser.
I did not review the addon, the other frontend files or the other invariants.
I did not check whether a dragend or Escape cancellation reaches the frame as a dragleave.
